items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Neuroscience, Public Health, Biological Sciences, Health Sciences or related filed, OR an equivalent combination of education and experience
Minimum 1 year of clinical research experience
Experience supporting psychiatric, neurological, or clinical trials research
Experience working with FDA-regulated studies, IRB submissions, and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines
Experience interacting directly with research participants in a healthcare or research setting

The Semel Institute of Neuroscience and Human Behavior is seeking to hire a full-time Assistant Clinical Research Coordinator to join the Neuromodulation Division. The Neuromodulation Division is leader in Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) and other innovative neuromodulation therapies for mood disorders and chronic pain. Our team combines cutting-edge research with exceptional patient care to deliver the latest evidence-based treatments. You will contribute to the overall operational management of clinical research activities from design, set up, conduct, throughout closeout. Key responsibilities include:
Assist with the coordination and day-to-day conduct of clinical research studies
Recruit, screen, and schedule study participants, and support the informed consent process
Collect, enter, and maintain study data and research records
Prepare and maintain regulatory documents and study files to ensure compliance with institutional and regulatory requirements
Coordinate study visits, protocol-required procedures, and research-related activities
Support reporting activities, quality assurance efforts, and study documentation
Collaborate with investigators, sponsor, research staff, and other stakeholders to support successful study execution
Please note: this position is 100% on site
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel
Interest in neuroscience, mental health, and innovative treatment approaches
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills
Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
Working knowledge of clinical research processes, human subjects research, and regulatory requirements
Ability to travel to and work at various clinic sites, meetings, conferences, etc.
